channel.title: GitHub Copilot Bulletin — English / Biweekly / Devs
channel.description: Latest GitHub Copilot updates for Devs (Biweekly, English)

item.title: Copilot Bulletin Biweekly #10 — July 15 to July 31, 2026 · Devs Edition
item.description: This period, Copilot deepened agent-native tooling and expanded model choice. Autonomous agents reached more of your workflow—the VS Code Agents window, Linear, GitHub Issues—while code review gained MCP and skills support. For developers, the practical shift is matching the right model and agent to each task, with richer context flowing directly into everyday coding and review.

item.title: Copilot Bulletin Biweekly #9 — July 1 to July 14, 2026 · Devs Edition
item.description: The first half of July put agentic development front and center. New model choices, a generally available integrated browser, vision support, and deeper agent providers across VS Code and JetBrains gave developers more ways to delegate real work and stay in flow. The theme is practical autonomy: richer tooling that keeps you in control while agents handle more of the loop.

item.title: Copilot Bulletin Biweekly #8 — June 15 to June 30, 2026 · Devs Edition
item.description: This period, the agent-native tooling GitHub previewed at Build reached general availability and spread across editors. The desktop app and the CLI's redesigned terminal shipped as GA, JetBrains gained first-class Copilot agents, and model choice both widened and got simpler. For developers, agentic workflows are no longer preview experiments — they're production-ready wherever you code.

item.title: Copilot Bulletin Biweekly #7 — June 1 to June 14, 2026 · Devs Edition
item.description: This period, agentic development moved from experiment toward everyday infrastructure. Copilot's agent capabilities matured in parallel across the terminal, the IDE, and a new desktop app, while larger context windows and configurable reasoning gave those agents more room to work. For developers, the practical takeaway: running, steering, and trusting agents across surfaces is becoming part of the daily workflow.

item.title: Copilot Bulletin Biweekly #6 — May 15 to May 31, 2026 · Devs Edition
item.description: The May 15–31 period was defined by one overarching theme: Copilot becoming a genuinely multi-surface, self-directing workflow platform for developers. A new frontier model arrived across every IDE, the model selection layer got smarter, and developer sessions became portable across devices — all reinforcing that the in-editor code assistant era is giving way to something more systemic.

item.title: Copilot Bulletin Biweekly #5 — May 1 to May 14, 2026 · Devs Edition
item.description: The first two weeks of May mark an acceleration in agentic development infrastructure. A dedicated GitHub Copilot desktop app arrives as a new surface for parallel agent sessions. The cloud agent becomes programmable via REST API. JetBrains users gain the CLI agent in public preview. VS Code ships four weeks of agentic improvements. The pattern: more surfaces, tighter control, less switching between tools.

item.title: Copilot Bulletin Biweekly #4 — April 15 to April 30, 2026 · Devs Edition
item.description: This fortnight marks a decisive expansion in how developers choose and control AI in Copilot. GPT-5.5 joins the model roster, BYOK opens the door to any provider, and agentic mode reaches JetBrains—while Visual Studio deepens its cloud agent integration with a dedicated debugger workflow. Model choice and autonomous assistance are now woven into every major IDE.

item.title: Copilot Bulletin Biweekly #3 — April 1 to April 15, 2026 · Devs Edition
item.description: The past two weeks reveal a clear pattern in Copilot's evolution: greater developer autonomy and mobility. VS Code gained a fully autonomous Autopilot mode, the CLI shed its dependency on GitHub-hosted models with BYOK support, and agent sessions can now be monitored and steered remotely from any device. Copilot is becoming less tied to a single desk or tool.

item.title: Copilot Bulletin Biweekly #2 — March 23 to April 6, 2026 · Devs Edition
item.description: The past two weeks mark a clear inflection point in Copilot's agentic story for developers. From parallel agent dispatching in the CLI, to a new SDK for embedding agentic workflows in any application, to verified commits and expanded IDE tooling—these updates form a cohesive foundation for developer-led AI automation. The tools to delegate, build, and trust agents are converging.

item.title: Copilot Bulletin Biweekly #1 — March 2 to March 16, 2026 · Devs Edition
item.description: The past two weeks mark a turning point in Copilot's agentic capabilities. Both VS Code and JetBrains IDEs shipped major agent upgrades — hooks, plugins, memory sharing, custom agents — while GPT-5.4 landed with stronger multi-step reasoning. Copilot is moving from code assistant to programmable development partner.
